name: Sumerian City-State Governance
description: City-states ruled by an ensi (governor) or lugal (king), with a council of elders and assembly of citizens. Temples played central economic and administrative roles.

name: Sumerian Social Stratification
description: Three-tiered society: free citizens (lu), dependent laborers (mushkenum), and slaves (urdu/geme). Temple and palace households were major employers.

name: Roman Republican Government
description: Complex system of elected magistrates, the Senate, and popular assemblies. Designed with checks and balances to prevent tyranny. Cursus honorum defined political career progression.

name: Roman Social Orders
description: Rigid social hierarchy: patricians, equestrians, plebeians, freedmen, and slaves. Social mobility possible through military service, commerce, or patronage.

name: Roman Law
description: Evolved from the Twelve Tables through jurisprudence into a comprehensive legal system. Distinguished between ius civile (citizen law) and ius gentium (law of nations).

name: Athenian Democracy
description: Direct democracy where male citizens participated in the ekklesia (assembly). The boule (council of 500) prepared legislation. Officials chosen by lot (sortition) or election.

name: Greek Paideia
description: Education system emphasizing gymnastics, music, reading, and rhetoric. The gymnasium served as center of intellectual life. Sophists and philosophers offered advanced education.

name: Aztec Triple Alliance
description: Confederacy of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan. The huey tlatoani of Tenochtitlan held supreme power. A complex bureaucracy administered tribute, justice, and warfare.

name: Aztec Social Stratification
description: Hierarchical society with nobles (pipiltin), commoners (macehualtin), serfs (mayeque), and slaves (tlacotin). Meritocratic advancement possible through military achievement.

name: Inca Administrative System
description: Highly centralized empire divided into four suyus. Decimal administration system organized population into units of 10 to 10,000. Quipu used for record-keeping.

name: Inca Social Hierarchy
description: Society divided into royalty, nobility (by blood and privilege), and commoners organized into ayllus (kin-based communities). Mit'a labor tax system redistributed labor.

name: Tang Imperial Bureaucracy
description: Centralized government with three departments (Secretariat, Chancellery, Department of State Affairs) and six ministries. Civil service examination system selected officials by merit.

name: Tang Examination System
description: Imperial examination system testing knowledge of Confucian classics, poetry, and statecraft. Created meritocratic path to official positions and social mobility.

name: Angkorian Divine Kingship
description: God-king (devaraja) system with the monarch as earthly representative of Hindu/Buddhist deities. Elaborate court hierarchy with royal officials administering provinces.

name: Angkorian Religious Organization
description: Syncretic Hindu-Buddhist religious system with elaborate temple hierarchies. Brahmins served the court while Buddhist monks maintained monasteries. Temple estates controlled vast resources.

name: Great Zimbabwe Political System
description: Centralized state governed by a paramount chief from the Hill Complex. Controlled gold trade and cattle wealth. Regional centers administered outlying territories.

name: Songhai Imperial Administration
description: Large West African empire with centralized government. Emperor (askia) ruled through provincial governors and a professional bureaucracy. Incorporated Islamic legal traditions.

name: Timbuktu Islamic Scholarship
description: Major center of Islamic learning with the University of Sankore and numerous madrasas. Scholars produced manuscripts on theology, law, astronomy, and medicine.

name: Carthaginian Government
description: Oligarchic republic with two elected suffetes (judges), a senate of wealthy elders, and a popular assembly. Military commanders appointed separately from civil authority.

name: Achaemenid Imperial Administration
description: Vast empire divided into satrapies (provinces). The King of Kings ruled through satraps, with royal inspectors (Eyes and Ears of the King) ensuring loyalty. Royal road system enabled communication.

name: Achaemenid Military
description: Professional standing army centered on the 10,000 Immortals. Multi-ethnic forces organized by nationality. Sophisticated logistics supported campaigns across vast distances.

name: Indus Valley Governance
description: Remarkably uniform urban planning across vast area suggests centralized or highly coordinated governance, though specific political structures remain unknown. Absence of palaces or monumental royal architecture.
key_roles: undetermined - no deciphered written records of governance

name: Teotihuacan Collective Governance
description: Evidence suggests collective or corporate governance rather than individual kingship. Apartment compounds may have housed lineage-based groups. No clear royal imagery in art.
key_roles: undetermined - possibly collective leadership|compound head|temple priest|merchant leader

name: Catalhoyuk Household Organization
description: Densely packed houses with standardized layouts suggest egalitarian social organization. Burials under house floors maintained ancestral connections. No evidence of centralized authority.

name: Natufian Semi-Sedentary Society
description: Early transition from mobile foraging to sedentary life. Small communities with emerging social complexity. Elaborate burials suggest nascent social differentiation.
